knowledge.content: The agencies charged with implementing the statute—the FDIC, the Federal Reserve, the OCC, and the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS) (collectively, the Federal banking agencies)—first issued joint regulations in 1978 to implement the statute.

Since then, the Federal banking agencies (including the OTS until 2011) have revised the CRA regulations several times and have provided guidance on the interpretation and application of the CRA regulations through the Interagency Questions and Answers Regarding Community Reinvestment.

On April 3, 2018, the U.S. Department of the Treasury released recommendations, based on stakeholder input, to modernize the CRA regulations. Moreover, on October 19, 2020, the Federal Reserve published an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPR) to solicit public input regarding modernizing the Federal Reserve’s CRA regulatory approach.

The issuing bank is the entity that authorizes the use of a prepaid card. Typically, the issuing bank is identified as the bank whose name is printed on the back of the prepaid card. This can include commercial banks, savings associations, credit unions, and branches of foreign banks.

A third-party program manager is responsible for designing, managing, and operating a prepaid card program. This entity contracts with a bank to issue prepaid cards under the program and handles transaction processing, customer service, and card distribution.

The responsibilities of an issuing bank, as outlined in the guidance, are distinct from any requirements under the Bank Secrecy Act.
